title: A1-14 · The imperfect to the plural; the denial withلَا‎

blocks.text: A1-14 · The imperfect to the plural; the denial with ⁧لَا⁩
Lesson overview

We study, we work, they live in Rome, we don't speak Arabic. With this unity complete the imperfect, adding the plural and the dual, and learn to deny it by ⁧لَا⁩ . You will also see a rule that surprises the Italians: when the verb precedes a plural subject it remains to the singular ( ⁧يَدْرُسُ الطُّلَّابُ⁩ • students study •). Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 34–35 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-14), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. to unite the imperfect in all thirteen persons;
2. grant the verb with a plural subject before and after the verb;
3. deny the present with ⁧لَا⁩ and respond negatively;
4. use verbs ⁧يَتَكَلَّمُ⁩ , ⁧يَتَعَلَّمُ⁩ , ⁧يُرِيدُ⁩ , ⁧يَقُولُ⁩ , ⁧يَزُورُ⁩ and other frequent verbs;
5. understand a text about a family and a dialogue with negative phrases;
6. tell what you do and what you do not do and your family or your group.
Two-week plan.

rows: Dialogue 1 · section 1: the plural and the dual of the imperfect
Section 2: the agreement with the plural subject · exercises 2–3
Section 5: ⁧لَا⁩ … ⁧وَلَا⁩ ; what negation for what · exercises 7–8
Module Review A1.3 for the test

blocks.text: 1. Dialogue 1 · How do you study?

Yūsuf: We read the lessons and write the exercises.

Salmā: Do you listen to dialogues every day?

Yūsuf: Yes, we listen in the car or at home.
Salmā: And you two, Mary and Hudā?
Māryā: naḥnu nadrusu maʿan. naqraʾu n- nuṣūṣa wa-natakallamu bi-l-ʿarabiyya.

⁧هُمَا يَعْمَلَانِ فِي المَكْتَبِ⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ . ⁧نَفْسِهِ، وَيَتَكَلَّمَانِ بِالعَرَبِيَّةِ أَحْيَانًا⁩

blocks.text: What to notice. Forms in -ūna ( ⁧تَدْرُسُونَ⁩ , ⁧تَسْمَعُونَ⁩ ) are the plural 'voi', with ⁧نَ⁩ - ( ⁧نَقْرَأُ⁩ , ⁧نَكْتُبُ⁩ ) are "noi" , in -āni ( ⁧يَعْمَلَانِ⁩ ) are the dual "their two" . In ⁧نَسْمَعُهَا⁩ "We listen to them" the pronoun is feminine singular (-hā) because it refers to dialogues, a plural of things (A1-15). ⁧المَكْتَبُ نَفْسُهُ⁩ The same office is: ⁧نَفْس⁩ + suffix after the name =
2. The Complete Imperfect

They (f.) ⁧يَعْرِفْنَيَعْمَلْنَيَدْرُسْنَْنَ⁩ … ⁧يَ⁩ How to remember her. There are only four prefixes: ⁧أَ⁩ (I) ⁧نَ⁩ (us), ⁧يَ⁩ (Him, their males), ⁧تَ⁩ (all the rest). There are four suffixes: -īna (Tu f.), -āni (dual), -ūna (male plural), -na (female plural). Forms in -ūna and -āni are the most frequent after the singular ones. The three particular verbs of A1-13 the following table is followed: ⁧نُحِبُّ، تُحِبُّونَ، يُحِبُّونَ⁩ (with prefix in u); ⁧نَأْكُلُ، يَأْكُلُونَ⁩ (the double hamza is only in ⁧آكُلُ⁩ ); ⁧نَقْرَأُ، يَقْرَؤُونَ⁩ (the hamza goes up wāw before ū; there is also the spelling ⁧يَقْرَأُونَ⁩ ).
3. Word and plural subject

rows: The verb before the subject remains singular; only agrees in the genre
The verb after the subject generally accords and number

blocks.text: Implicit subject . ⁧يَدْرُسُونَ فِي المَكْتَبَةِ⁩ The verb alone contains the subject:

Because. When the verb comes first, the subject that follows already says who acts and how many are: the verb does not repeat it. When the subject has already been said, the verb that follows takes it back with an embedded pronoun (-ūna, - na). In journalistic texts you will find above all the first type: ⁧قَالَ الوُزَرَاءُ⁩ ... "The ministers have said... "with the verb to the singular. The dual works in the same way: ⁧يَعْمَلُ الزَّمِيلَانِ هُنَا⁩ / . ⁧الزَّمِيلَانِ يَعْمَلَانِ هُنَا⁩
4. New verbs

⁧يَبْحَثُ عَنْ⁩ search ⁧يَبْحَثُونَتَبْحَثِينَأَبْحَثُ⁩ The way they're used. ⁧يَتَكَلَّمُ⁩ + language to the accusative ( ⁧أَتَكَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ⁩ (I speak Arabic) or ⁧بِـ⁩ + language to the genitive ( ⁧نَتَكَلَّمُ بِالعَرَبِيَّةِ⁩ We speak in Arabic. ⁧يُرِيدُ⁩ + name to the accused: ⁧أُرِيدُ قَهْوَةً⁩ I'd like a coffee. ⁧هَلْ تُرِيدِينَ شَايًا؟⁩ ; with a verb (I want to study) you need a building that you will see in A2. ⁧يَقُولُ⁩ introduces a direct discourse: ⁧يَقُولُ المُدِيرُ⁩ «…». ⁧يَبْحَثُ⁩ He wants ⁧عَنْ⁩ : ⁧أَبْحَثُ عَنْ مِفْتَاحِي⁩ . Shapes and roots. ⁧يَتَكَلَّمُ⁩ and ⁧يَتَعَلَّمُ⁩ have the prefix ⁧تَ⁩ - and the double (form V); ⁧يُرِيدُ⁩ and ⁧يُسَاعِدُ⁩ have the prefix in u (forms IV and III); ⁧يَقُولُ⁩ , ⁧يَزُورُ⁩ , ⁧يَعِيشُ⁩ have a long vowel in the middle because the second consonant of the root is ⁧و⁩ or ⁧ي⁩ (Verbs - concave) The verbal forms you will study in B1: For now learn every verb with its three key forms (I, you f., them).
5. Denial with ⁧لَا⁩
To deny a verb to the imperfect one puts ⁧لَا⁩ before the verb. Nothing else changes.

- No... or... ⁧لَا أَشْرَبُ القَهْوَةَ وَلَا الشَّايَ⁩ I don't drink coffee or tea. Answer no. ⁧لَا، لَا أَفْهَمُ⁩ No, I don't understand. ⁧لَا⁩ is the answer, the second denies the verb. Three denials for three structures. Each structure has its own denial:
Word to the Perfect ⁧مَا⁩ ( A1), ⁧لَمْ⁩ ( A2) ⁧مَا ذَهَبْتُ⁩ A1-18

Very useful formulas. ⁧لَا أَعْرِفُ⁩ Not less than € 65,7 ⁧لَا أَفْهَمُ⁩ I don't understand. ⁧لَا أَتَكَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ جَيِّدًا⁩ I don't speak Arabic well. ⁧لَا بَأْسَ⁩ It's okay. It's okay.A1-01). Use them immediately with your interlocutors.
6. Dialogue 2 · A lost tourist
A firm Jordanian tourist Hudā In front of the station.

rows: as-sāʾiḥ: ʿafwan, hal tatakallamīna l- ʿarabiyya?
Excuse me, do you speak Arabic?
Hudā: naʿam, qalīlan. abī tūnisī. mā l- muškila?
Hudā: Yes, a little. My father is Tunisian. What's the matter?
as-sāʾiḥ: abḥaṯu ʿan funduqī, lākin lā aʿrifu l-ʿunwān.
Tourist: Looking for my hotel, but I don't know the address.
Hudā: What is the hotel's name?
as-sāʾiḥ: lā aḏkur. huwa qarībun min maḥaṭṭatin kabīra.
Tourist: I don't remember. It's near a big station.
Hudā: hunāka maḥaṭṭatāni kabīratāni hunā! hal maʿaka miftāḥu l-ġurfa?
Hudā: Here are two big stations! Do you have the room key with you?
Hudā: ʿalayhi smu l-funduq. funduquka amāma l-maḥaṭṭati l-markaziyya.
Hudā: Above is the name of the hotel. His hotel is in front of the central station.
as-sāʾiḥ: šukran ǧazīlan! lā aʿrifu Mīlānū ǧayyidan.
Tourist: Thank you very much! I don't know Milan well.
Hudā: lā baʾs. ahlan wa-sahlan fī Mīlānū!
Hudā: It's okay. Welcome to Milan!

blocks.text: What to notice. The tourist uses female forms ( ⁧تَتَكَلَّمِينَ⁩ , ⁧تَفَضَّلِي⁩ ) because he talks to Hudā. ⁧لَا أَعْرِفُ⁩ , ⁧لَا أَذْكُرُ⁩ : Denial before the verb. ⁧جَيِّدًا⁩ the accused acts as an adverb: "Bene" , "Bene" .
7. Pronunciation

-ūna and -na. yadrusūna (u long) and yadrusna (no vowel before -na): listen to the difference in script B. Pause: yadrusūn , yadrusn(a) . The double of ⁧يَتَكَلَّمُ⁩ . yatakallamu : the double l; The accent falls on -kal- . Long vowels from concave. yaqūlu , yazūru , yaʿīšu , yurīdu : Keep them long. ⁧لَا⁩ + verb. It reads as a unit: lā aʿrif , lā yatakallam . Don't pause.
8. New lexicon

rows: I don't know ( ⁧لَا⁩ denies the imperfect)
⁧المَكْتَبُ نَفْسُهُ⁩ The same office is the same

blocks.text: Notes of use. ⁧يُرِيدُ⁩ is the verb to ask with courtesy: ⁧أُرِيدُ⁩ ... I'd like... in shops and restaurants you can also hear ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكَ⁩ + name. ⁧يَقُولُ⁩ to the perfect ( ⁧قَالَ⁩ ) is the most frequent verb of the press: you will see it in A1-18. ⁧نَفْس⁩ means "same" when following the name with the suffix ( ⁧المَكْتَبُ نَفْسُهُ⁩ ), “soul, self” on its own. ⁧يَذْكُرُ⁩ also means "to name": ⁧لَا يَذْكُرُ التَّقْرِيرُ الاِسْمَ⁩ The report does not mention the name
